text:
alex_ux: Hey - trying to get redwoodctl installed on a Windows 10 laptop (MSI v0.12.1). Installer runs, says complete, but redwoodctl isn't on PATH and the Start Menu shortcut doesn't work. Anyone seen a silent failure like this?

ravi_devex: Which installer did you use, alex_ux? x64 MSI from releases.redwood.ai?
alex_ux: Yep, downloaded the 64-bit MSI from the release page. No UAC prompts besides the usual. I ran it as my normal user, not explicitly elevated.

jen-install: Quick check: can you open C:\Program Files\Redwood or C:\Program Files (x86) and see if redwoodctl.exe exists? Also check %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp for installer logs (redwood-install-*.log).
alex_ux: There's no Redwood folder under Program Files. I found a temp dir: C:\Users\alex\AppData\Local\Temp\redwood-installer-3456 and it has redwoodctl.exe but Windows Defender shows a recent quarantine entry.

pat_sre: Defender heuristics often quarantine unsigned binaries from temp folders. If the installer extracts payload to temp and the AV quarantines it during install, the final copy to Program Files never happens. Check Windows Security -> Protection history.

alex_ux: Yep, quarantined with reason: Potentially unwanted application. Restored it and tried the installer again, but same result (no Program Files copy).

ravi_devex: Workaround: run the MSI as Admin and disable real-time protection temporarily before running. Long-term fix: we're going to sign the binary and adjust installer staging. For now you can manually move the exe:

  1) Restore from quarantine to temp folder.
  2) Move redwoodctl.exe to C:\Program Files\Redwood\redwoodctl.exe
  3) Add C:\Program Files\Redwood to your PATH (System Properties -> Environment Variables)
  4) Run: "redwoodctl version" to confirm.

jen-install: If your profiles didn't migrate, check %APPDATA%\Redwood\profiles.json. Sometimes the installer fails to write the profile when the main binary is quarantined.

alex_ux: My profiles.json is missing. I had localserve tokens in there for local testing. Oops.

pat_sre: If you still have the old profile on the machine (from a previous user dir) you can import it:

  redwoodctl profile import --file "C:\Users\alex\AppData\Local\Temp\redwood-old-profiles.json"

If you don't, we can re-auth and recover local tokens via redwoodctl login --scopes local:serve (but tokens are ephemeral so you might need to re-run local tests).

alex_ux: Re-running login just goes into a loop: opens browser, completes auth, browser redirects to local callback but redwoodctl says "login complete" then immediately "auth refresh required" and prompts again. Happening on PowerShell and cmd.

ravi_devex: That sounds like a redirect URI mismatch. Which redwoodctl version? We fixed a callback parsing bug in v0.12.2. You're on 0.12.1, right?
alex_ux: Yes, 0.12.1.

jen-install: Try updating to the canary build we pushed with the auth fix. It includes two things: better callback parsing and a short retry backoff to avoid infinite loops. To grab it: https://staging-releases.redwood.ai/canary/redwoodctl-0.12.2-canary.msi (internal only)

ci-bot: deploybot: canary installer with auth/callback fix was pushed to staging at 2026-03-20T14:12:00Z :rocket:

pat_sre: For folks hitting this in corp networks with strict proxies, add these to Defender/AV exclusions if you can't disable protection:
  - %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\redwood-installer-*
  - C:\Program Files\Redwood\*
  - redwoodctl.exe (hash-based exclusion preferred)

ravi_devex: Action items for team: (1) Add installer payload signing (tracking: #STR-452), (2) update MSI to stage to Program Files before AV scan (STR-453), (3) backport auth callback parsing fix to stable (STR-454).

alex_ux: Thanks all — got the canary MSI, installer worked after temporarily disabling Defender. Profiles restored from backup and redwoodctl login completed cleanly on 0.12.2-canary. Leaving Defender exclusions in place for now.

jen-install: Filing a docs blurb for troubleshooting Windows installs (av quirks + manual migrate steps). I'll add a troubleshooting snippet for migrating profiles and for the login loop.

alex_ux: Appreciate it. If anyone else hits this I'll paste the Defender event IDs and the temp paths I saw. :thumbsup:
